Hi, I’m an M.Sc. student working on Lean 4 ecosystem design.

I recently wrote a paper titled “xLaDe: A Lean 4 Ecosystem Framework,” which explores repository structure, experiment isolation, and workflow design around Lean 4.

I’m planning to submit it to arXiv, but my university doesn’t have researchers in this area, so I’m not sure how to find an appropriate endorser.

I’d really appreciate any guidance on how people in the Lean community usually approach this.

Project repo: https://github.com/LakshitSinghBishtTM/xLaDe

Happy to share the draft if helpful.

Thanks!
Asking for endorsement in public forums isn’t allowed for arxiv , your best bet would be to ask your professors’ extended networks
@Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 Thanks for the clarification. I’ll try to find an appropriate endorser through the usual channels.

Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 said:

Asking for endorsement in public forums isn’t allowed for arxiv

That's news to me. I just reviewed the arXiv instructions and I see that it says, "Please note, however, that it is inappropriate to email large numbers of potential endorsers at once," but I don't think that is the same as asking for endorsement in a public forum.

The purpose of the endorsement system is, or should be, to stem the influx of garbage. It's not an end in itself, but a necessary evil in a world full of people acting in bad faith, as well as people who may be well-intentioned but are (for lack of a better word) cranks. Even if the arXiv were to update their policy to explicitly discourage soliciting endorsers in a public forum, I don't think we, as participants in this forum, should just blindly follow the arXiv guidelines. Instead, we should decide for ourselves whether to allow such requests in our forum.

In my opinion, if someone appears to be doing the kind of Lean-related work that is appropriate for the arXiv but is encountering difficulties finding an endorser because they are insufficiently well-connected socially, then there is nothing inappropriate about asking here for help finding an endorser. From personal experience, I know that finding an endorser can be an annoyingly difficult task, and that there are other shortcomings of the endorsement system. Unless this Zulip becomes flooded with inappropriate requests for help finding an endorser, I don't see why we should have a ban.

Just mirroring what I have seen moderators say, I am not a moderator.

Mostly took it for granted , I personally have no particular view. I have no endorsement or moderation capacity of any sort, sorry if it was misrepresented

Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 said:

Just mirroring what I have seen moderators say, I am not a moderator.

Okay, if it's a policy that the moderators of the Lean Zulip have decided on, that's different. The way your previous comment was phrased made it sound like it was an arXiv policy for "public forums" in general, not just the Lean Zulip.

I would be interested in seeing previous discussion of this policy, if someone can point me to it.
@Kim Morrison can assist perhaps , though I don’t remember active discussions just seeing arxiv endorsement shut down as such.

Thanks to Snir Broshi for the pointer. If the moderators have made that decision, that is certainly their prerogative. I am still surprised that "asking for arXiv endorsements in public fora is explicitly against arXiv's terms." Did I miss something in the arXiv instructions?
Note that also arxiv endorsement links allow the reader to negatively endorse you, which is motivation for sending them only to people you actually collaborate with
It's perhaps also worth noting that submitting from an academic (.edu, .ac.uk, ...) rather than personal email address can often bypass the endorsement need.

Eric Wieser said:

It's perhaps also worth noting that submitting from an academic (.edu, .ac.uk, ...) rather than personal email address can often bypass the endorsement need.

This is no longer true, due to a recent change in policy.

Let me say a little bit more about why I think fans of Lean, and more generally of formal methods, should pay close attention to arXiv policies.

I believe that mathematical rigor is a democratizing force. It enables independent researchers to know that what they have done is correct, without having to solicit a nod of approval from someone with high social status. The formal methods community is uniquely well positioned to advocate for independent researchers, since we have powerful tools for determining whether an independent researcher (with potentially low social status) has something of value to offer.

The arXiv faces the Herculean task of cleaning up the Augean mass of AI slop and other nonsense. It is understandable that they are raising the bar for submission higher and higher. I won't pretend to have a panacea for their troubles, but I do think we should be aware that the endorsement system is far from ideal. Among other things, it amounts to relying on the "old boy network" to determine who gets in and who stays out. In that sense, the endorsement system is "anti-democratic." As I said before, it's at best a necessary evil, and not a good thing in and of itself.

If someone approaches the formal methods community with independent Lean-related research, and asks for assistance to get past the arXiv gatekeepers because they don't have high enough social status, what should our response be? Should we just say, "Sorry, go away; you need to use the old boy network"? In my opinion, no. Once again, the endorsement system is not, or at least should not be, regarded as an end in itself, but as a means toward the goal of keeping low-quality material out of the arXiv. If we have the capacity to make assessments of quality ourselves, then why not do so (by permitting people to solicit an endorser here), rather than blindly follow the letter of the law?

We shouldn't be surprised that the arXiv, in response to various pressures, is increasing the barriers to entry, even if it comes at a cost to the wider community. Despite strong objections by several well-established mathematicians, the arXiv went ahead and implemented their policy to require English-language submissions. They are in the process of becoming an independent non-profit with a CEO whose salary is estimated to be around $300,000. That may be a good thing, but there's no guarantee that the new CEO will always implement policies that are in the best interests of the scientific and mathematical community. In my opinion, we all need to do our part to ensure that the arXiv remain the stellar scholarly resource that it has been for the past 35 years. In some cases, that might mean bending the arXiv's "rules" for the benefit of the community as a whole.

I appreciate you all for the thoughts and info. I also want to add that I first tried the same way and asked my maths and cs profs and none of them have published on arxiv earlier (journals only), so noone from my uni can endorse me. Also, noone from their network is able to endorse me. So, I am stuck as I literally can't find anyone to endorse.
I also checked arxiv policies and it said that endorser just needs to check if the submitter is actually someone who is genuinely doing research, and its not a peer-review of paper so I thought to post here, also a clarification I have asked how do lean4 researchers find the endorsers, I am not asking for direct endorsement.

Update2: On 6 august, paper got rejected because I am in masters and they said need a minimum of Ph.D. (written in mail)
